summary: The three OOMKilled restarts of notification-service this week are best explained by dep-5402 (v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00Z), which added an in-memory ConcurrentHashMap template cache on the email render path and is the only notification-service change in the window; a steady, unbounded-looking memory ramp begins ~2h after it and repeats on a ~24h cadence to the ~95-98% ceiling, each time collapsing into an OOMKill (F1, F13, F10, F9, F7, F8, F12). The reporter's "consumer choking on a replay" theory is not supported: consumer lag spikes follow each crash rather than precede it, the ramps predate the 2026-03-23T18:00Z Kafka maintenance, and retention is a stored-data-window setting rather than a capacity knob (F11, F15, F7, F9). Confidence is medium (0.60) because attribution to the cache is by timing and elimination only — no heap/absolute-memory metric or runtime profile confirms the cache is the allocator, and broker-side rebalance events are not queryable. The immediate priority is to roll back dep-5402 and confirm the sawtooth stops; a replay/rebalance cause remains the principal runner-up and should be discriminated by heap profiling and broker-side consumer-group checks.

ranked_hypotheses.title: dep-5402 in-memory template cache leaks/unbounds memory
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The code release dep-5402 v3.8.0 on 2026-03-21T00:00Z added an in-memory ConcurrentHashMap template cache keyed by template+locale+userSegment on the email render path. The key space grows unbounded (or entries are never evicted), so resident memory ramps steadily ~24h until the container hits its limit and is OOMKilled; the daily cadence reflects the time to fill the heap from reset, and the consumer lag spikes/email delays are consequences of each crash (in-flight work lost, redelivery), not causes.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5402 v3.8.0 (in-memory template cache) deployed to notification-service at 03-21T00:00Z
Memory begins a steady ramp from ~48% baseline starting 03-21T02:00, ~2h after the deploy
Heap climbs to >90-98%, full-GC warnings, then sawtooth crash to ~48% at each OOM
OOMKilled exits (137) recur ~24h apart as the cache refills
Consumer lag spikes and email delays appear AFTER each crash, not before

assumptions: The template cache grows unbounded / lacks eviction, and it is the dominant allocator of the growing heap
No tracked heap/limit change accompanied dep-5402 (GAPS)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Broker-side Kafka rebalance/replay storm (HIST-104 class)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A Kafka broker-side event (partition reassignment/rebalancing storm, as in HIST-104) causes consumer-group churn and a replay/backlog flood to notification-service, driving unbounded in-memory buffering and OOM. The reporter's 'consumer choking on a replay after maintenance' is a variant of this.

causal_chain.claim: Kafka maintenance/broker-side rebalance changes consumer-group state
Consumer receives burst of stale/replayed records and buffers them in memory
Memory ramps to limit and container is OOMKilled
Consumer lag spikes as backlog grows

assumptions: A broker-side rebalance/replay occurred (not queryable via config/deploy tools)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Directly contradicted: consumer lag spikes FOLLOW the memory crash, not before (F11), so backlog cannot be the cause of the ramp. The ramp begins ~2h after the deploy on 03-21 and repeats ~24h apart predating today's maintenance (F7/F9/F12). Kafka maintenance is at 03-23T18:00Z, after the second and third ramps already began (F15). Mem still ~48% at start and ramps steadily, not stepwise from a replay burst.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Cyclical traffic peak (end-of-day trade confirmations) with no faulty change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The OOMs are a regular traffic-driven cycle tied to daily end-of-day trade-confirmation volume; the sawtooth reflects periodic traffic peaks filling the heap, unrelated to Kafka maintenance or any code change.

causal_chain.claim: Daily EOD trade-confirmation burst raises memory use
Memory peaks to limit and container OOMKilled ~24h apart

assumptions: Traffic alone can fill heap to 95-98% (no traffic metric pulled - GAPS)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The pattern does not predate dep-5402: baseline was flat ~48% before 03-21 (F10), and the first ramp/deploy align within ~2h (F13/F10). A load-driven cycle would have shown the same pattern earlier and would not correlate with the single code change adding an in-memory cache.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka retention reduction (cfg-2410) increased broker memory/backpressure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The Kafka log.retention.ms reduction (7d->3d) at 03-23T18:00Z changed broker behavior (e.g., compaction/segment churn or backpressure), increasing notification-service memory pressure and causing the third OOM.

causal_chain.claim: Reduced retention triggers segment deletion/compaction pressure on broker

assumptions: Retention reduction affected broker memory/backpressure in ways that reach the consumer
The change preceded symptom onset meaningfully
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Retention is a stored-data-window setting, not a consumer/broker-capacity knob (F15). The change is ~2h before the third OOM, but the same OOM pattern occurred on 03-21 and 03-22 BEFORE any Kafka change existed (F7/F8), so it cannot explain the series. No notification-service config change exists (F14).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource-limit/heap config was lowered, narrowing OOM margin
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A JVM heap (Xmx) or container memory-limit config change narrowed the headroom so the steady ramp reaches the limit sooner, producing the OOMKilled events.

causal_chain.claim: Heap or container memory limit was reduced
memory_pct ramp hits ceiling faster -> OOMKilled

assumptions: Such a limit is tracked but was missed (GAPS)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: get_config_changes with scope=notification-service returned count=0, not partial (F14); the only config change anywhere is the Kafka retention (F3). No evidence a limit change occurred. Behavior is explained by memory growth, not a lowered ceiling.

facts.statement: The only notification-service deployment in the window (2026-03-16..24) is dep-5402 v3.8.0 at 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z, 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' (ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment on the email render path), status live with rolled_back_at null — the sole notification-service change preceding the first OOM at 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z.

Exactly three OOMKilled restarts (exit code 137) of notification-service-7d9f occurred, at 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z and 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z, roughly 24h apart; the cumulative restarts metric steps 0->1->2->3 in the matching hourly buckets.
memory_pct shows a sawtooth ramp-then-crash before every OOM: from a ~48% reset it climbs to 95%+ (max 97.37% on 03-21, 97.98% on 03-22, 98.44% on 03-23) and resets to ~46-48% at each restart.

Baseline memory was flat ~48% before 03-21; the ramp clearly begins in the 2026-03-21T02:00 bucket (~2h after dep-5402), with the first log anomaly being 'GC pause 253ms exceeded 200ms target' at 2026-03-21T03:00:44Z and heap-over-90% 'full GC took' warnings starting 2026-03-21T21:37:01Z, just before the first OOM.

consumer_lag spikes immediately AFTER each memory crash, not before: lag stays in its normal ~50-100 band during the ramps, then jumps (03-21T22:00 avg 2273.11/max 17161.92; 03-22 20:00 and 22:00 buckets; 03-23 19:40 avg 4578.25/max 18137.93 while memory is already at 96.73%).

The Kafka maintenance cfg-2410 (log.retention.ms 604800000 -> 259200000, 7d -> 3d, platform-team) is timestamped 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z — ~2h before the third OOM and ~19h after that cycle's memory ramp had already begun; retention is a stored-data-window setting, not a consumer/broker-capacity knob.
There is no configuration/flag change on notification-service in the window (scope=notification-service returns count=0, not partial); the sole config change anywhere is the Kafka retention change.

No code deployment at all occurred on 2026-03-23 (12:00-24:00, all services: count=0, not partial); the last deployment of any kind was the unrelated auth-service v7.1.4 jackson bump on 2026-03-22T13:00Z, and the only other deployment in the window across all services is that auth-service patch.

notification-service has no incoming service edges (no caller); its load arrives only by consuming from the shared Kafka topic. Its direct dependencies are kafka (queue-consume) and email-provider (external, no telemetry).

Kafka is a shared component (shared: true, owner platform) with settlement-service as a peer consumer, so a shared-Kafka change could reach settlement-service — but the retention reduction is the only Kafka change and neither settlement-service nor the other peers (order-service, payment-service) is reported with OOM symptoms.

assumptions: The dep-5402 template cache (ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment) grows without effective eviction and is the dominant allocator of the growing heap; this is inferred from timing and elimination, not from runtime attribution, since no heap/absolute-memory metric or profile was available.

No notification-service heap (Xmx) or container memory-limit change accompanied dep-5402 that would narrow headroom; the config-change query returned no notification-service entries, but such settings may simply not be tracked there.
no unlogged Kafka broker-side rebalance/replay occurred around 03-21..03-23; broker-side events are not queryable via the config/deployment tools, so absence of a config record does not exclude one.
The ~24h cadence reflects the time needed to fill the heap from reset under steady traffic, rather than a daily traffic or maintenance trigger; no traffic metric was pulled to confirm this.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) The third OOM repeats the identical sawtooth shape of the 03-21 and 03-22 events, with heap-over-90% warnings minutes before the kill (03-23 ramp warnings from 18:34:46Z, OOM at 19:59:21Z); the reported link to today's Kafka maintenance is not supported because the ramp began the prior day.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) The only historical incident matching the symptom pair (lag spike + delayed emails) is HIST-104 (2025-11-05), attributed to a Kafka broker rebalance/partition-reassignment storm — a broker-side event class with no deployment/config change; no prior OOMKilled/memory-ramp incident for notification-service was found.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back dep-5402 (notification-service v3.8.0 in-memory template cache) to the previous release, or disable the template-cache code path via its flag/fallback, to stop the memory ramp.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5402 is the only notification-service change in the window and the ramp begins ~2h after it, with three ~24h OOM cycles and no notification-service config change to explain them (F1, F13, F10, F9, F14). Backing it out is the direct mitigation and also the discriminating test.

recommended_actions.action: Verify the rollback by watching memory_pct and restarts on notification-service-7d9f through at least the next ~24h cycle window: memory should stay near the ~48% baseline and restarts should stay flat (no 0->1 step).
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure signature is a clear sawtooth to 95-98% with a ~24h fill time; holding flat at baseline through one full cycle confirms the mitigation (F9, F7, F8).

recommended_actions.action: While rolled back or immediately after, capture a heap dump / bound the cache: confirm the ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment is the dominant retained set and add an eviction policy (size cap and/or TTL) or switch to a bounded cache.
recommended_actions.rationale: Attribution to the cache is currently by timing and elimination only; a heap profile converts the medium-confidence inference into direct evidence and closes the main gap (F1, F13).

recommended_actions.action: Run the discriminating check for the runner-up hypothesis: inspect Kafka consumer-group state and broker-side partition reassignment/rebalance activity for the notification-service group (and settlement-service as peer consumer) across 03-21..03-23, and confirm whether any replay volume burst preceded a ramp.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 (broker rebalance/replay) is the rejected-but-plausible alternative and broker-side events are not queryable via config/deploy tools; lag increases after crashes and ramps predate the maintenance, but an unlogged rebalance cannot be excluded without this check (F11, F15, F6, F18, F17).

recommended_actions.action: Pull the adjacent-service anomaly sweep that was budget-exhausted (kafka broker and trade-service/order/payment/settlement) for OOM, lag and latency anomalies in the three OOM windows to confirm only notification-service is affected.
recommended_actions.rationale: The claim that only notification-service is affected is currently unverified, and a shared-Kafka effect on peers would indicate a different root cause (F4, F17).

recommended_actions.action: Add heap/absolute memory (used vs limit) metrics and JVM heap-size tracking for notification-service, plus alerting on the memory-ramp slope rather than only on OOM restarts.
recommended_actions.rationale: Only memory_pct was available, so heap vs working-set could not be quantified and the ramp was only detected at crash; slope alerting converts this class of leak into an early warning (F9).

recommended_actions.action: Add CI guardrails requiring bounded/eviction-configured in-memory caches and a memory-leak soak test gating deploys on the email render path, and track JVM/heap and consumer settings in get_config_changes so headroom changes are auditable.
recommended_actions.rationale: The unbounded in-memory cache reached production unremarked and no heap/limit change was trackable, which is why attribution rested on timing and elimination (F1, F13, F14).

data_gaps: No heap/working-set absolute byte metric was available for notification-service (only memory_pct), so heap vs working-set breakdown and absolute memory limits could not be quantified and attribution of the growth to the template cache is by timing/elimination, not runtime profiling.

No notification-service consumer/Kafka-consumer-group, JVM/heap (Xmx) or container resource-limit config change appears in get_config_changes (count=1 overall, not partial); cannot confirm whether headroom tuning accompanied dep-5402 or such settings are simply untracked.

Kafka broker-side events (partition reassignment/rebalance, as in HIST-104) are not queryable via the config/deployment tools, so absence of a config record does not exclude an unlogged broker-side rebalance around 03-21..03-23.

email-provider has has_telemetry=false and no time-series metrics were pulled for notification-service/kafka, so exact lag values and short-window onset order of lag vs memory could not be established from raw series.

Neighbouring services (kafka, trade-service) could not be queried for OOM/lag/latency anomalies in the same windows (budget exhausted), so the claim that only notification-service is affected is unverified, and it is unknown whether the Kafka maintenance/replay reached the broker.

The notification-service log query returned 40 of 48 matches (truncated: true); the final 8 entries 2026-03-23T18:49-19:59 were not retrieved, though a separate ERROR-only query captured all three OOM events.

Historical search returned only HIST-104 and HIST-107; no prior HIST entry with literal 'OOMKilled' for notification-service was retrievable, so the 'third this week' history and any prior replay-triggered OOM precedent could not be independently established.

No change is recorded between 2026-03-21T00:00Z and 03-23T12:00Z besides the Kafka retention change, so the ~24h cadence of the three restarts has no attributable triggering change other than the shared dep-5402 code path.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A heap dump or profile showing the retained memory is NOT dominated by dep-5402's template cache (e.g. dominated by consumer buffers or deserialized messages) would refute H1 and move the rebalance/replay class (H2) to the top.
The memory ramp persisting at the same ~24h cadence and reaching the same 95-98% ceiling after dep-5402 is rolled back would falsify H1 as the cause of the series.

A broker-side partition reassignment/rebalance or replay-volume burst confirmed (via consumer-group and broker telemetry) to precede the ramps — rather than follow the crashes — would restore H2 despite the config-tool blind spot.
Discovery of a tracked, timestamped notification-service heap (Xmx) or container memory-limit reduction narrowing headroom would support the rejected H4 and change the mitigation to a config revert.

Evidence that settlement-service and/or other Kafka peers (order-service, payment-service) show OOM or lag anomalies in the same windows would point to a shared-Kafka cause rather than a notification-service code change.

Evidence that memory growth is traffic-volume-coupled (a traffic metric showing end-of-day trade-confirmation peaks driving the ramp and the same sawtooth predating dep-5402) would support the rejected H5 cyclical-traffic explanation.

A deployment/config change artifact not visible in the reviewed queries (e.g. rollback of dep-5402 having actually occurred, or a dep-5402 tag mismatch) that breaks the alignment between dep-5402 and the first ramp would weaken H1's central timing evidence.
